gaps.note: The page never says what c[P] means (presumably c times the 0/1 truth value of the predicate P, so the update happens only when c=1 and P holds). The eight additions, the cycle claims and the identity (u',w') all depend on this unstated convention.

gaps.quote: hence a bijection of the rectangle
gaps.note: The page never describes the rectangle (the array of M records, indexed by the x, y, z chunks and spectator fields, in lexicographic order), nor the spectator coordinates, so the reader does not know what is being permuted. A_rect is also named after it without explanation.

gaps.quote: One line on all segments is a cyclic shift of a whole chunk by an offset independent of the target chunk
gaps.note: The page asserts that each simultaneous line equals one cyclic shift mod 2^L but never gives the shift. The paper (line 2071-2074) gives y <- y + eps*sum_{i=0}^{f-2} 2^{j_i}[x_{j_i}=1][z_{j_i}=b] mod 2^L. Without it the reader cannot check that it is a cyclic shift or that its offset does not depend on the target.

The page never says why each segment moves by at most eight. The paper (lines 2049-2052) notes each coordinate is updated four times by at most one, so displacement is at most four, and eight is a weaker bound. The reader is also not told that a segment staying in [0,2^K-1] is what rules out carries between segments.

gaps.quote: For $0\le i<f-1,$ the $K$ bits of $y$ from position $j_i$ form a segment
gaps.note: The page treats only the f-1 positions j_0..j_{f-2}, yet the opening claims the XOR on all f selected bits. The paper (lines 2054, 2187-2193) omits the top position j_{f-1} so the segments stay disjoint, then does it at the end with a two-bit elementary stream operation costing O(V). When f=1, S_0 and T_0 are identities. The page never says T_0 acts only at j_0..j_{f-2}, or how the last bit is handled.

gaps.quote: There are exactly twenty excluded values for each guard among $2^{K-1}.$
gaps.note: Missing hypothesis K>=6 (paper line 1976; also 0<=rho<K). Excluded values are g<10 and g>2^{K-1}-11, ten each. They are disjoint, and 20 <= 2^{K-1}, only when K>=6. For small K the count 'exactly twenty' is false. The page never states K>=6.

gaps.quote: and $T_0$ preserves $\mathcal B,$ so $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B.$
gaps.note: The page gives no reason T_0 preserves B. The paper (line 2107) says T_0 preserves all guard values, since it only flips the low bit a_i of each segment and leaves the guard bits g_i, h_i unchanged. The page never states what T_0 does beyond calling it the ideal XOR map. The complement argument S_0(B^c)=T_0(B^c)=B^c, S_0(B)=B is also omitted.

gaps.quote: The repair extracts the records at $\mathcal B$ with destination-rank keys, stably radix-sorts them, and reinserts them in one scan.
gaps.note: The page does not say what the destination is (q'=T_0(S_0^{-1}(q)), computed by reversing the eight additions), how the rank of q' comes from rank(q) and the chunk differences (paper lines 2164-2177), or why sorting and reinserting implements T_0 after S_0. Distinct keys are not enough for a one-scan reinsertion; the keys must be exactly the ranks of the vacated positions (paper line 2183), which follows from T_0S_0^{-1} permuting B.

gaps.term: cost of scans and radix passes
gaps.quote: record scans $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3+V),$ radix passes $O(|\mathcal B|A_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect})).$
gaps.note: The page does not explain where the cube of A_rect comes from (schoolbook arithmetic on O(A_rect)-bit counters per record, paper lines 2161-2163, 2168-2169) or why there are at most A_rect radix passes over records of R+A_rect bits (paper lines 2196-2197). The reader must take these terms on trust.
